correctness.rationale: The claim is reduced to the standard uniform transition expansion for the regularized incomplete Gamma function, using Temme's complex-variable remainder control and Cauchy estimates to justify one derivative of the uniform expansion. After setting \(\delta=\kappa-1\), \(\varepsilon=\sqrt\delta\), and \(r=\delta\alpha\), the expansion gives the explicit functions \(A(r)=\sqrt r+1/(3\sqrt r)\) and \(B(r)=-r^{3/2}/6-\sqrt r/2-1/(12\sqrt r)+1/(540r^{3/2})\). A global localization argument excludes \(r\to0\) and \(r\to\infty\). The unique minimum of \(A\) is \(r=1/3\); differentiated next-order expansion gives the offset \(7/45\), and substitution gives the stated cubic correction. No finite computation is used to establish the asymptotic theorem.

value.rationale: The lead paper explicitly identifies \(\kappa=1\) as an interesting phase transition and supplies only numerical minimizers above the transition. The new result gives the critical exponent, the exact divergence scale of the optimizer, and two next-order constants, quantitatively explaining the published \(\kappa=1.01\) data. This is a natural structural refinement of a stated phenomenon, not an arbitrary parameter slice or table recomputation.
